title: The Hearthwife's Almanac
author: Goodwife Aldith Ashwick
pages: Brightwake: put out the hearth on the first morning and carry home a coal from the Kindlehall. A fire lit from a neighbour's coal is borrowed luck, and borrowed luck must be paid back by Reaping.
For a threshold ward: salt along the sill, a sprig of rowan over the lintel, and a candle that has burned at a death-vigil. Say the names of everyone who sleeps in the house. Leave no one out.
Fever: willow bark steeped long, honey, and cool cloths. If the sick one dreams of a door, wake them gently and keep a light burning. Do not let them sleep alone that night.

A black thread knotted on your doorframe is ill-wishing. Do not cut it. Burn it whole in a blessed fire, then go and make peace with whoever you quarrelled with last. The curse breaks when the grudge does.
Leaffall: count your stores. One sack of grain for each mouth for each month of winter, and one more for the stranger at the door. The hearthkin notice who is turned away.
Deepnight: keep a light in the window on the longest night, relight the candles on your family's graves, and do not answer a knock you did not expect after the bell. Open in the morning instead.
